sections.advice: Use Hannover north gate → Burgdorf fuel gate as clean positioning. Keep it tidy, ignore impatient traffic and save the enthusiasm for the good road ahead. The value here is not drama; it is arriving at the riding section with space, fuel and concentration intact.

sections.advice: The forest part from Burgdorf fuel gate to Celle river road rewards quiet precision. The road may look empty, but surface changes and animals do not care about your schedule.
sections.photoQuery: Burgdorf fuel gate Celle river road Hannover / Lower Saxony escapes

sections.advice: Celle river road → Bergen heath edge is the reward section in Hannover. Look through the bends, use legal pull-offs for photos and keep a little margin for tractors, cyclists and damp shade. The best ride here is smooth, not noisy.
sections.photoQuery: Celle river road Winsen Aller water stop Hannover / Lower Saxony escapes

sections.advice: Bergen heath edge → Winsen Aller water stop is shade riding: beautiful, cooler and sometimes slick. Expect damp patches, leaves, gravel and wildlife where the trees meet the road.
sections.photoQuery: Bergen heath edge Wietze coffee return Hannover / Lower Saxony escapes

sections.advice: Treat Winsen Aller water stop → Wietze coffee return as bend craft. Brake early, look high through the turn, and keep throttle changes gentle. It is more satisfying to link ten clean bends than rescue one silly one.

dolomites-sella-ronda-overnight-scout-pa.slogan: Campolongo Pass to Chur · one way, about 544 km back to the start

waypoints.name: Campolongo Pass
waypoints.advice: Campolongo Pass is where the day begins. Reckon on about 8 °C colder than the valley, and more in the wind. Next is Gardena Pass, climbing 261 m.

waypoints.name: Gardena Pass
waypoints.advice: You top out at 2136 m here. The road climbs 261 m on the way up to it, steadily. Reckon on about 10 °C colder than the valley, and more in the wind. Nothing on this route is higher. At this height the road is a summer one: snow gates can stay shut into June and shut again in October. Next is Val Gardena overnight base, mostly downhill.

waypoints.name: Val Gardena overnight base
waypoints.advice: 363 km in you reach Val Gardena overnight base. You lose 576 m on the way down to it, steadily. Reckon on about 6 °C colder than the valley, and more in the wind. Next is Back to Chur, mostly downhill.

waypoints.name: Back to Chur
waypoints.advice: Back to Chur closes the day. You lose 967 m on the way down to it, steadily.

Val Gardena overnight base → Back to Chur drops about 967 m over 212 km. Brakes and eyes forward; the views are behind the corners, not in them.

scenicChapters.title: Great Dolomites Road
scenicChapters.narrative: The last of the trees go and the road runs out onto open ground. The summit sits at 2136 m, and what surrounds it is rock, weather and distance — cold comes early up here and stays late. Ride it with something in reserve: the summit is not the end of the work, only the middle of it.
scenicChapters.riderNote: Check the pass is open before you commit to it.

scenicChapters.title: Stelvio Pass
scenicChapters.narrative: 506 km that neither climbs nor drops much. The road settles into the ground rather than fighting it. This is where a day makes up time without anyone trying. Third and fourth, and very little else.

dolomites-sella-ronda-overnight-scout-pa.story: 544 km from Corvara in Badia to Chur, about 8 h 36 of riding. The climb of the day is Gardena Pass. It tops out at 2,136 m. It crosses from Italy into Switzerland - carry ID and check vignette or toll rules. It is a high-mountain day.

scenicChapters.title: Grand Tour of Switzerland
scenicChapters.narrative: For 34 km this is Grand Tour of Switzerland, a road with a name of its own and a reason for it — expect company on a summer weekend. Early is better than fast.

scenicChapters.title: Grand Tour of Switzerland
scenicChapters.narrative: Water arrives beside the road and stays for 37 km. The line follows the shore because there is nowhere else for it to go. Slow enough to look. The surface follows the shoreline, so the corners arrive where the water decided, not where an engineer did.
